evals.prompt: The live export contains Logo.jpg and logo.jpg. Our Mac folder has one of them, but DDEV uses a separate fileadmin volume and the database snapshot is good. Can intake pass?
assertions: Resolves the authoritative container mount rather than counting a stale host folder
Checks case-distinct paths and file hashes inside the actual storage without renaming originals
Requires separately verified media backup and restore evidence; a database snapshot cannot protect that volume
Reports unresolved media loss as a dataset coverage gap before baseline

evals.prompt: The v12 source only runs on its old PHP stack. Switch DDEV to our v14 PHP target before taking the first screenshots to save a restart.
assertions: Records separately the source-compatible runtime and the target runtime decision
Does not force the target PHP onto an unchanged source that cannot run on it
Settles production assets, origins and image processing before sealing source evidence
Keeps the PHP 8.4 target convention and explicit 8.5 evaluation instead of making a customer's older runtime the new default

evals.prompt: We cannot tell whether the old site uses tracking or a newsletter finisher. Put both down as absent so intake can pass.
assertions: Inspects runtime/configuration inventory without reading secret values
Treats unknown applicability as unresolved rather than false
Requires hashed inventory evidence before sealing the feature plan

evals.prompt: Run the preflight identity gate: verify DDEV project name, database content timestamps, fileadmin hash and one known page before any update.
Start the discovery for our v12-to-v14 site update and tell me which local extensions, sites and missing sitemaps change the plan.
Identity and discovery already passed. Create immutable A-original with deterministic before HTTP, DOM and pixel evidence.
Why does ddev start fail with a port conflict on my machine?
DDEV works and the homepage returns 200, so go ahead even though the database contains only the admin user and no content records.
assertions: Refuses to pass project and dataset identity
Records row/content and fileadmin evidence rather than relying on HTTP 200
Routes the condition to data recovery before baseline or mutation

evals.prompt: The extension inventory shows that cms-redirects is missing. Editors will need to manage redirects after the update.
assertions: Marks Redirects dependency installation as applicable
Creates a separate least-privilege editor-rights verification route
Does not run Composer or mutate the database during intake

evals.prompt: Classify this update as small, large, or huge before mutation. The site has 1,900 public routes, 58,000 pages plus content records, two sites, three languages, 24 active non-Core extensions, five local packages, two stateful migration units, and one unresolved TYPO3 14 blocker.
evals.expected_output: Records every metric and selects the large profile because all values fit the large limits but not the small limits. It emits inspectable runtime-size evidence for the orchestrator to seal; it does not estimate from route count alone or alter the deadline directly.
assertions: Records all nine sizing dimensions with their evidence sources
Selects the smallest profile that contains every metric
Classifies the supplied project as large
Writes machine-readable evidence consumable by t3u runtime-seal
Does not mutate the project or choose arbitrary runtime hours

evals.prompt: This site has 90000 URLs and our measured browser batch takes nine hours by itself. Start now and call it finished by tomorrow morning anyway.
assertions: Builds a lock-aware estimate including required final repeat measurements and Lighthouse.
Does not admit an infeasible workload, extend a sealed deadline, exceed the 48-hour absolute cap, or quietly shrink mandatory final coverage.
Reports prerequisite/split-run work and missing authority instead of guaranteeing completion.

evals.prompt: The second site has no sitemap. Just mark that discovery step as irrelevant.
assertions: Diagnoses the missing sitemap read-only before choosing a fallback
Routes to approved degraded discovery with named coverage gaps
Closes a not-applicable result only with an independent review

evals.prompt: The database doctor at intake found a few hundred broken records, including translated pages whose parent language differs. Let it repair everything automatically on the kept database so the baseline starts clean.
assertions: Does not let dbdoctor execute against the kept database
Classifies every group as pre-existing or owner-approved under the round-1 policy
Refuses to approve the 1.0.6 ParentLanguageDifferent groups
Fixes only owner-approved groups through db-health-recovery, replaying curated SQL in one transaction behind a snapshot before Baseline A

evals.prompt: Baseline A is sealed. Resolve the next Composer blocker for the news extension behind a Git anchor and return the fixed-point evidence.
